fixes.explanation: Yes! Verse 7 says, “May the righteous flourish in his days…” Right before it, verse 6 asks for the king to be “like rain that falls on freshly cut grass, like spring showers that water the earth.” The prayer asks for the righteous to flourish in his days, and that fits the picture of rain on the earth.

Struggling isn't what the prayer asks for, friend. Verse 7 says, “May the righteous flourish in his days…” Verse 6 has just asked for the king to be “like spring showers that water the earth.” The prayer asks for flourishing, not struggling.

Scattering is more like a bag of sprinkles hitting the floor. Verse 7 asks, “May the righteous flourish in his days…” Verse 6 has just asked for the king to be like spring showers that water the earth. The prayer asks for flourishing.

That's right. Verse 10 says, “May the kings of Tarshish and distant shores bring tribute; may the kings of Sheba and Seba offer gifts.” These are kings from far-off places, and the prayer asks them to come with their hands full. Tribute and gifts are what it asks for.

You're picturing a whole fleet showing up, friend. But verse 10 asks for the kings of Tarshish and distant shores to bring “tribute,” and for the kings of Sheba and Seba to offer “gifts.” No soldiers are mentioned. I think the prayer is asking for giving, not fighting.

The kings do bow and bring gifts in the prayer, so I see why you'd go there. But verse 12 turns in a new direction. It says, “For he will deliver the needy who cry out and the afflicted who have no helper.” Nothing here about rewarding the kings.

I can see why that one sounds believable, but it's False. Verse 12 says he will deliver “…the afflicted who have no helper.” No helper means nobody in their corner, and the prayer says the king helps them anyway.

Tribute shows up in verse 10, but it's not the reason here. Verse 14 says, “He will redeem them from oppression and violence, for their blood is precious in his sight.” The reason the verse gives is that their blood is precious in his sight. Tribute isn't mentioned there.
Yes! Verse 16 says, “May there be an abundance of grain in the land; may it sway atop the hills.” That's more than a little. The prayer asks for an abundance, and for it to sway atop the hills.
Verse 16 doesn't say that. It asks for “…an abundance of grain in the land…” The prayer says in the land, not for the king alone. Nothing in the verse limits the grain to one pantry.
